data.name: Eulaliah
data.long_meaning: The name Eulaliah is derived from the Latin word eulaleia, which means 'delightful, pleasant, beautiful'. In Christian tradition, this name is often associated with the biblical figure Eulalia, a young girl who was martyred for her faith in Rome during the 3rd century.

in_hebrew.name: אולליה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אולליה מורכב משתי מילים עבריות: 'אל' שמשמעותו אלוהים, ו'לל' שמשמעותו משפט או שיר. השם אולליה ניתן למי שנושא את שיר האל או משפט האל. השם מופיע בתנ"ך כחלק מהמסורת היהודית והנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Εὐλαλία
in_greek.meaning: Εὐλαλία, ἡ εὐσέβεια καὶ ἡ πραότητα
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Εὐλαλία προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὸν ἑλληνικὸ λόγο καὶ σημαίνει 'καλὴ εὐσέβεια' ἤ 'πραότητα'. Στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη, τὸ ὄνομα Εὐλαλία συνδέεται μὲ τὴν εὐσεβεια καὶ τὴν ἀρετή. Ἡ Εὐλαλία ἦταν μία ἀπὸ τὶς πρώτες Χριστιανὲς μάρτυρες.

in_latin.name: Eulalia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Eulalia derivatum est ex Graeco 'Εὐλαλία', quod significat 'bona fama' vel 'suavitas'. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Eulalia erat usitatum inter Christianos, qui virtutem et sanctimoniam significare volebant.

historical_references.reference: Eulalia of Merida, also known as Eulalia of Mérida, was a virgin and martyr venerated in the Catholic Church. Her legend relates that she was a daughter of a nobleman in Merida, in the Roman province of Lusitania. During the Diocletian Persecution in the late 3rd or early 4th century, she was tortured and imprisoned for her refusal to give up her Christian faith. After her release, she continued to preach and convert others to Christianity. Eventually, she was arrested, tortured, and executed. Her feast day is celebrated on December 12.
historical_references.context: Roman province of Lusitania during the Diocletian Persecution

historical_references.reference: Eulalia of Barcelona, also known as Santa Eulàlia, was a virgin and martyr venerated in the Catholic Church. According to legend, she was born in Barcelona in the late 3rd century. She was a wealthy young girl who lived an austere and devout life. During the Diocletian Persecution, she was denounced for her Christian faith and was subjected to various tortures, including being burned in a bath house. She survived and continued to preach Christianity. She was eventually beheaded and is now the patron saint of Barcelona.
